rapidfolio.notes: Light coverage of bottom-up product adoption and employee-to-team expansion weakens adherence to the B2B Adoption Before Procurement thesis.

withasync.notes: The memo underplays founder execution fit despite a low score, offering no rationale or evidence-linked discussion of team capacity or track record.

prescience-inc.notes: Rationale leans on positioning and team credentials rather than deeply arguing adoption dynamics (workflow habit, employee-to-team expansion). It could tie evidence more explicitly to how bottom-up usage grows pre-procurement.

os3.notes: It omits the analysis’s explicit risk about unproven manufacturing/logistics/support readiness, focusing instead on shipment timing.

archal.notes: Rationale leans on generic market tailwinds and competitor validation rather than tightly arguing each adoption dimension.

assemble.notes: Rationale leans on product merits and team strength rather than explicitly arguing adoption mechanics (e.g., employee-to-team expansion and procurement path). Make the core rationale map more directly to the five “B2B Adoption Before Procurement” pillars.

datoric.notes: The rationale slightly drifts into generic competition (Appen/Scale) rather than strictly B2B adoption-before-procurement levers.

dream.notes: The rationale focuses on product, competition, and founders rather than explicitly arguing employee-to-team expansion and the enterprise procurement path. It underweights how workflow habit translates into bottoms-up adoption and expansion.

induction-labs.notes: Rationale centers on research and benchmark claims rather than tying evidence to adoption-before-procurement pillars (workflow habit, team expansion, and enterprise path).
